back: Estimated selling price less the costs to complete and sell the goods.
Lower of cost and net realisable value, applied item by item (or group by group).
Purchase price plus costs of bringing goods to their present location and condition (e.g. carriage inwards).

front: Why lower of cost and NRV?
back: Prudence: expected losses recognised now; profits only when goods are sold (realisation).
Cost of sales understated; gross profit, profit for the year, current assets and equity overstated.

front: Effect of the error next year
back: This year's closing inventory is next year's opening inventory, so next year's profit moves the opposite way.

front: Is carriage outwards part of inventory cost?
back: No: it is a selling expense. Carriage inwards is part of cost.
Opening inventory + purchases + carriage inwards − returns outwards − closing inventory.
